text:
Autistic people have long been described as lacking empathy. The double empathy problem, named by Damian Milton in 2012, suggests understanding can break down on both sides when people with very different ways of being interact.

A 2024 study tested one side. Non-autistic adults watched autistic and non-autistic people describe emotional events. They found autistic narrators' emotions harder to track, especially happiness and sadness.

For anyone supporting autistic people, this invites humility. An emotion that seems unclear may reflect a mismatch in expression and reading, not an absence of feeling. Building rapport, rather than assuming a lack of understanding, is a useful starting point.

Where the evidence stops:
• Only four narrators and no autistic viewers, so one direction was tested.
• All narrators were White and highly educated.

Key sources:
• Cheang et al., 2024: https://doi.org/10.1177/13623613241252320
• Milton et al., 2022: https://doi.org/10.1177/13623613221129123
